title: Threat Modeling: The Power of Trust Boundaries

scenes.say: Ever wonder where attackers usually break into systems? Let’s talk about trust boundaries—the number one place threats get in.

scenes.label: DFD
scenes.sub: Maps how data moves and where trust changes
scenes.say: First, draw a data flow diagram. This maps how data travels and highlights where trust shifts—those are your trust boundaries.

rows.b: Can data be changed in transit?

scenes.say: At every trust boundary, apply STRIDE. Ask: can someone fake who they are, change data, or see things they shouldn’t?
Mitigate threats at these boundaries with validation, encryption, and authentication. Track each fix, and make sure it’s verified before launch.

scenes.question: What’s most often missed in threat models?
scenes.right: Missing trust boundaries—where attackers cross in
scenes.say: Here’s a common interview trap: teams list threats but skip marking trust boundaries. That’s where attackers sneak in.
